title: Bolivia Crisis Tracker Update — Aug 26, 2026
summary: President Paz dismissed censured Economy Minister José Gabriel Espinoza on Aug 21 after Congress voted 91-129 to remove him over a skipped budget interpellation, naming Óscar Mario Justiniano interim minister; the government disputes the censure's constitutionality. Phone chats recovered from Fernando Cerimedo's device reportedly show a contact tied to intelligence chief Erik Correa González messaging in real time during the Aug 17 attack on Nadia Beller, who now calls the shooting a "state crime" and is demanding Paz respond publicly. Evo Morales said he was advised to wear a bulletproof vest amid his assassination-plot claims, and cocalero federations mounted an armed vigil warning security forces not to move against him ahead of an Aug 26 rally in Ivirgarzama. Separately, the government signaled it may revise the unpopular Supreme Decree 5676 diesel-price hike after backlash from large consumers.

title: Bolivia Crisis Tracker Update — Aug 23, 2026
summary: Fernando Cerimedo, an Argentine consultant informally credentialed as President Paz's "principal adviser," was ordered into 180 days of preventive detention at Palmasola prison after a Santa Cruz judge cited phone messages allegedly showing he ordered the Aug. 17 shooting of former partner Nadia Beller. Beller says she was targeted after threatening to expose corruption reaching the Paz family; the government has since distanced itself, denying Cerimedo ever held a formal state position beyond campaign-era digital consulting. The episode adds political pressure on Paz nine months into his term, alongside the unresolved COB truce and pending IMF-linked reforms.

title: Bolivia Crisis Tracker Update — Aug 21, 2026
summary: The government raised diesel prices 84% for large industrial consumers (Supreme Decree 5676, Aug 17) while keeping the subsidized Bs. 9.80/L rate for transport and households, aiming to curb cross-border fuel smuggling. The floated boliviano's official exchange rate climbed to Bs. 12.13/$1 after the Jul 31 central bank fixing. Evo Morales publicly accused President Paz and Defense Minister Justiniano of a U.S.-backed plot to kill him in Chapare; Justiniano denied the claim and demanded evidence. Also backfilled President Paz's Aug 6 independence-day address, in which he touted a falling country-risk index and a $940M restitution to Bolivians.
